recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If a future work group wants Binary to enumerate RDF/Turtle or other FHIR MIME types locally, handle that as a new broader content-type consistency issue rather than as an unapplied part of FHIR-17027.
issue_request: FHIR-17027 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 technical correction for Binary asking that the REST wording not imply application/fhir+xml and application/fhir+json were the only FHIR content types.
initial_application: The issue was applied by svn revision 14345, represented by git commit b460ed645c6342e838cc9178950807b4cb0d06a1, which added explicit non-exhaustive wording after the XML and JSON MIME-type examples. The same-day FHIR-13507/FHIR-16886 rewrite in 4c0d34042c3e8742eda89fdb336da09c622aa009 recast the text as a request with a FHIR type in Accept, with XML and JSON as examples.
additional_context: Binary is active in the current build and is part of the infrastructure normative package. The current Binary note says requests with a FHIR type in Accept return the Binary in the requested FHIR format and refers to standard FHIR mime types for _format; the HTTP page contains the broader current MIME-type guidance, including RDF/Turtle. The later FHIR-37381 duplicate-bullet cleanup preserved the current first bullet. No directly relevant Zulip or Confluence record was found.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source is already non-exhaustive through the phrase "FHIR type" and its example-only XML/JSON list, so adding "etc" or enumerating every FHIR MIME type would be redundant and would not change implementer understanding.
